preamble: In Central and Northern Swedish and in Eastern Norwegian, which have an alveolar /r/, a rhotic followed by /s/ fuses with it into a single retroflex fricative [ʂ]. The apical rhotic carries its retraction onto the sibilant and is itself lost, in parallel with /rt, rd, rn, rl/ > [ʈ, ɖ, ɳ, ɭ]. The process applies across word boundaries and is absent from southern varieties with uvular /r/ and from Finland Swedish.

examples.note: Passive of föra 'bring'; /rs/ realized as a single retroflex fricative.
Fusion also applies across a word boundary. Southern varieties with uvular /r/ do not retroflex.
Eastern Norwegian rs > [ʂ]; some speakers have [ʃ].
